Chief Complaint: This 36 year-old female was referred to the fine needle 
aspiration clinic by Dr. Kevin Hughes for consultation and diagnosis of a mass 
in the left breast. 
 
Clinical History: 36 year-old pregnant female with history of left breast 
excisions for papillomas, now with 2 left breast masses on ultrasound. 
 
Review of Symptoms: 
Constitutional: Well-developed, well-nourished adult in no apparent distress. 
Allergy to lidocaine: No. 
Medications/anticoagulants: Patient is not on blood thinners. 
 
Social History: 
Tobacco use: No. 
Alcohol use: No. 
 
Past Medical History: 
No personal history of malignancy. 
 
Review of Patient Data in the EMR: 
Radiology: Yes. 
Past Histology: No. 
Office Notes: Yes. 
 
Physical Examination: Laterality was established according to departmental / 
universal protocol. Examination of the left breast reveals a 1.2cm  firm, 
mobile mass. 
 
Assessment: Based on the clinical history and physical examination, an FNAB is 
warranted. 
 
Procedure: The procedure and complications were explained to the patient and 
written consent was obtained. 3 aspirates were performed using 25 gauge needles 
without anesthesia and without complications. 4 slides were stained for 
immediate evaluation; additional tissue was submitted for further evaluation. 
 
Disposition: The immediate interpretation findings were discussed with the 
patient. The preliminary results were communicated to Dr. Hughes in person at 
4:55 p.m.
